title: Quasi-finite affine decomposition after a surjective base change
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be a quasi-finite morphism [pqf-def-quasifinite] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). There exist an affine scheme $U\prime$, a surjective morphism $a:U\prime\to U$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V\prime=V\times_U U\prime$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product] which is surjective on underlying points (a thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]), such that the composite $Z\xrightarrow{i}V\prime\to U\prime$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-open finite-presentation theorem, applied to the whole source and target as affine opens, makes $B$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Index the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$ by inclusion; their union is $A$, and the union has the ring-colimit universal property since a compatible family of ring maps is defined element by element. The index is a small nonempty directed set: adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives an upper bound. Apply finite-presentation descent to obtain $B_0$ finitely presented over some $A_0$, with $B\cong A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$. The affine quasi-finiteness descent lemma gives a later stage $A_i\to B_i$ which is quasi-finite. Put $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $h_0:V_0\to U_0$. Both schemes are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and hence Noetherian by the cited theorem. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $h$ with the pullback of $h_0$ along $U\to U_0$. We construct the required cover for $h_0$ in steps 2-9, then pull it back in step 10.

proof.text: Convert the Stacks quasi-finite predicate to Mathlib LocallyQuasiFinite using the discrete-fibre characterization. Apply the existing source-library finite stratification theorem over the Noetherian affine base. Partition each stratum into reduced affine immersed schemes. Their finite coproduct T is affine and Noetherian and maps surjectively to the base. The pullback becomes finite because this is true on each open-and-closed summand, by pullback pasting and target locality.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof of part (1)

proof.text: For each finite affine map $Y_t\to S_t$, apply the section-cover lemma. It gives a surjective finite locally free $A_t\to S_t$, a closed immersion $Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t\hookrightarrow W_t$, and finitely many closed sections $s_k:A_t\cong W_{t,k}\subseteq W_t$ covering the underlying space of $W_t$. The scheme $A_t$ is affine and Noetherian: a finite algebra is of finite type (module generators also generate it as an algebra), so finite-type preservation of Noetherianity applies to $A_t\to S_t$. Here $S_t$ is Noetherian: it is a closed subscheme of an open subscheme of the Noetherian $T$ of step 2, hence locally Noetherian (opens of locally Noetherian schemes are locally Noetherian, quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian), and affine, hence quasi-compact. Set $Y_{A_t}=Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Apply the disjoint closed-section partition theorem to the closed subscheme supplied by the finite affine section cover. It gives finitely many reduced affine base pieces whose pullbacks are covered by pairwise disjoint closed sections. This directly proves the Boolean refinement, reduced factorization, and selection steps; the original separate Boolean-refinement module and reduced-ideal lemma are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof of part (1)

proof.text: Take the finite coproduct of the base pieces and the finite coproduct of their selected sections. Each component inclusion of the base coproduct is closed as well as open: its complement is the union of the other open summands. Its pullback inclusion is therefore closed. The section maps into the total source are pairwise disjoint closed immersions. Their coproduct is a closed immersion: surjectivity on stalks is local at the source; injectivity follows from disjointness; and the map is closed because images of closed subsets are finite unions of closed images. Point coverage makes this a thickening. Its composite to the total base is finite, as the ambient map is finite, and etale, as each component composite is an isomorphism followed by an open coprojection. Source locality glues etaleness. No Chinese remainder theorem or special coproduct-of-copies lemma is used.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof of part (1)

proof.text: Reassociate nested pullbacks to compose the two surjective affine covers. Finally pull the thickening back along the original affine base U -> U_0. Pullback pasting identifies the composite finite etale morphism with its base change; surjectivity, closed immersion, finiteness and etaleness are stable under base change. The new base is affine as a fibre product of affines. The result has exactly the original theorem signature.
